D: A grumpy teacher, a grieving cook and a troubled student are stuck at a New England boarding school over Christmas 1970.
P: Serve dessert when Mr Hunham orders the cherries jubilee.
S: Mary's grilled cheese and tomato soup
Mary Lamb's school kitchen at Barton

Golden grilled cheese of vintage cheddar and mozzarella on buttered sourdough, cut into fingers for dunking in a smoky tomato soup. Fry 1 diced onion and 2 garlic cloves in 2 tbsp olive oil for 5 minutes. Add 2 x 400g tins crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1 tsp sugar and 300ml chicken stock and simmer 15 minutes, then blitz smooth and stir in 50ml cream. Butter 8 slices sourdough on the outside and fill with 150g cheddar and 100g mozzarella. Fry over medium heat for 3 minutes a side until golden. Cut into fingers.
the trip into Boston over the break

Creamy New England clam chowder with smoky bacon, potato, thyme and fresh clams, served in mugs with oyster crackers. Fry 3 diced rashers bacon until crisp, add 1 onion and 2 celery sticks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 2 tbsp plain flour, then 400ml fish stock, 300g diced potato and a few thyme sprigs and simmer 12 minutes. Add 1kg cleaned clams, cover and cook 4 minutes until open, then remove the shells. Stir in 300ml cream and heat through. Season with pepper and serve with oyster crackers.
M: Christmas for the three left behind at Barton

Roast chicken with bread and herb stuffing, crunchy roast potatoes, glazed carrots and gravy, a small Christmas dinner done properly. Fry 1 diced onion in 40g butter, mix with 150g fresh breadcrumbs, 2 tbsp chopped sage, the zest of 1 lemon and 1 egg, and stuff a 1.8kg chicken. Rub with butter and salt and roast at 200C for 1 hour 20 minutes. Roast 1kg halved potatoes in oil for 50 minutes. Glaze 4 carrots with 20g butter and 1 tbsp honey. Rest the chicken, then make gravy from the juices with 1 tbsp flour and 350ml stock.
W: the cherries jubilee at the restaurant

Dark cherries simmered in a buttery orange and brandy sauce, flamed at the table and spooned hot over vanilla ice cream. Drain a 680g jar pitted cherries, keeping 150ml syrup. Melt 30g butter with 60g brown sugar in a wide pan, add the syrup and the zest and juice of 1 orange and simmer 3 minutes. Stir in 1 tsp cornflour mixed with water, then add the cherries and warm through. Off the heat, pour in 60ml brandy, then carefully light it with a long match and let the flames die down. Spoon over 1L vanilla ice cream.
K: the bottle Mr Hunham keeps close

Bourbon with hot water, honey, lemon and a cinnamon stick, a warming nightcap for a New England winter. Plain honey lemon for non-drinkers. Boil 800ml water. In each of 4 heatproof mugs, put 1 tbsp honey, the juice of half a lemon, 45ml bourbon and a cinnamon stick. Top each with 200ml hot water and stir until the honey dissolves. Stud a lemon slice with 3 cloves and float it on top. Leave out the bourbon for anyone not drinking.
